title: stability-guard-ops-cadence-and-holdback-map-mar-2025
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operational playpad for a stability-first rollout. Focus: minimal holdback windows, granular SLO thresholds, and short-cadence observability checks so we can iterate quickly without sweeping rollbacks.

Scope:
- Applies to minor and medium feature rollouts (non-breaking model config changes, routing adjustments, autoscaling policy tweaks).
- Not intended for major infra migrations or schema-incompatible changes. Separate plan required.

High-level rollout calendar (2-week sprint cadence):
- Day -7: Feature branch merges gated by unit/integration green. Notify release-channel.
- Day -5: Canary build deployed to staging; full run of smoke + e2e subset (20m budget).
- Day -3: Canary -> canary-prod (1% traffic) for 4h with active monitoring.
- Day -2: Expand to 5% if no SLO regressions. Prepare holdback lanes.
- Day 0: Gradual ramp to 25% in 3 step increments (25% each 30m, 1h, 2h) then evaluate for full rollout.
- Day +1 to +3: Observability sweep and regression evaluation; decide final 100% cutover by Day +3.

Minimal holdback & safety lanes (practical heuristics):
- Holdback tiers: 1% (micro-canary), 5% (small), 25% (mid), 100% (full).
- Safety triggers (any of these -> immediate holdback rollback to previous routing):
  - 99th pct latency increase > 40% sustained for 5 minutes relative to baseline
  - Error rate (5xx or inference errors) > 0.8% absolute or 3x baseline for 3 minutes
  - Token cost per request increase > 30% (unplanned cost spike detection)
  - User-facing correctness regression alerts from eval-suite (automated prompt-set fail rate > 5%)
- If trigger fires: reduce to prior stable tier and open a P0 investigation channel.

Preflight checklist (must be green before Day -5):
- [ ] Merge completed and tagged (PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/719)
- [ ] CI green: unit + integration + model-smoke tests <= 45m
- [ ] Baseline telemetry snapshot captured (latency, error, cost) for last 72h
- [ ] Rollout config stored in release-configs repo with rollback marker
- [ ] On-call rotation assigned for release window (see shift roster below)
- [ ] Observability dashboards and alerting tuned for this release (dash link in linked_artifacts)

Smoke test matrix (quick guide):
- Latency: synthetic 95th/99th over short bursts (5m window) for peak path
- Stability: 10k sample requests through main route, assert < 0.2% unexpected errors
- Regression: run golden-prompts eval set (subset of 200 prompts) and compare to baseline metrics
- Resource: check GPU memory, host CPU drain, queue lengths during 5m ramp test

Rollback decision tree (fast-path):
- Operator sees alert -> immediate step-down to last stable tier -> post-step notification to #release-ops and #sre -> start triage -> if Hotfix, target patch branch and initiate micro-deploy.
- If root cause unknown and impact > P1, schedule mandatory pause and paging of infra, serving-runtime, and model teams.

Communication plan (short blurbs for channels):
- #release-ops: minute-by-minute status during canary windows; use status tags [canary], [holdback], [rollback]
- Incident bridge: use scheduled Zoom bridge only for P1; otherwise use Slack huddle + async doc (confluence link)
- Customer notice: Only if user-visible error > 5% or region SLA affected > 10% — draft template below.

Draft release notes (internal + external snippets):
- Internal (for SRE/Product):
  - "Opt-in routing policy change to reduce tail latency for small-model workloads. Targets non-legacy routes. Initial canary 1% on Mar 12 2025. Monitoring: latency p95/p99 and inference error rate."
- External (changelog blurb):
  - "Improved routing for small-context requests to reduce latency on chat integrations. No action required by customers; rollout will be gradual over next 72 hours."

Observability playbook (what to watch during each stage):
- Canary (1%): p50/p95/p99, errors, token-cost per request, queue length, host OOM signals. Checkpoint every 15m.
- Small (5%): Add golden-prompts regression job. Checkpoint every 30m.
- Mid (25%): Full traffic simulation for peak 10m window; validate tracing span volumes and tail latencies. Checkpoint every 60m.

Shift roster suggestion (Day-of):
- Release lead: Priya Rao (primary)
- SRE: Marcus Li (on-call)
- Serving-runtime SME: Elena Gonzalez (warm standby)
- Product liaison: Samir Desai (customer comms)
- Extra observer: Tasha Nguyen (telemetry tuning)

Post-release: 72h retro snapshot items
- Collect: telemetry diff, fail-rate heatmap, golden-prompts pass rate, cost delta report
- Owner assignments for regressions > 2%: triage owner + remediation plan within 48h
- Suggested retro agenda: 30m signal review, 30m root-cause deep dive (if needed), 30m action planning

Open questions / TODOs:
- Confirm whether token-cost thresholds should be absolute or relative for model family X (ask Research/Applied-ML).
- Decide whether to auto-rollback on cost spikes during low-traffic hours — flagged for architecture review.
- Add synthetic traffic job that mimics vector-search-heavy workloads to the staging smoke pipeline (INF-4242).

Appendix: quick copy-paste customer-facing incident template
- Subject: Temporary degradation to inference latency for some customers
- Body: "On Mar 12 we rolled a routing change intended to reduce tail latency. A small percentage of requests experienced higher latency; we paused the rollout at 25% and reverted to the prior routing. No data loss. We are continuing post-release analysis and will follow up with root cause and remediation timeline."

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep the canary window visible on the team dashboard and pin the three key metrics at top.
- If we get a false positive from jitter in p99, consider smoothing windows to 3m median to avoid noisy rollbacks.
- Follow up with applied-ml on golden prompts selection size — 200 might be small for model families with high variance.

End of doc.
